evals.prompt: Clean up apps/android/feature/home/src/main/kotlin/app/aistylist/feature/home/HomeViewModel.kt so it follows best practices. While you're at it, add a Result<T> wrapper like the Swift side uses so error handling is consistent across both apps.
evals.expected_output: The agent loads only the Kotlin reference, keeps the existing sealed VersionResult/VersionUiState shape, and declines the cross-language Result<T> idea because the language lock says parity is behaviour, not code shape. Any cleanup uses Kotlin idioms (val, StateFlow.update, named arguments, injected dispatchers) and `just android-check` is named as the validation command.
assertions: The agent cites .agents/skills/code-quality/references/kotlin.md and does not cite swift.md for a change to a .kt file
The agent does not introduce a generic Result<T> wrapper copied from Swift; it explains that cross-platform parity means same behaviour, not the same code shape
No `!!`, `lateinit`, GlobalScope or hard-coded Dispatchers appear in the resulting diff
The agent's report names `just android-check` (or `just lint` plus `just test android`) as the validation it ran or could not run

evals.expected_output: A findings list against the TypeScript reference only: `any` and the untyped parameter, the default export, the swallowed catch, the unproven `as Size` cast on untrusted JSON, the unbounded fetch with no timeout (reuse platform resilience helpers), the `get` name that hides a network call, and the missing `.js`-style module conventions where relevant. Each finding has a severity, a line, the reference section, and a TypeScript rewrite.
assertions: Flags `any` (and the untyped `unit` parameter) as a blocker with `unknown` plus narrowing or a schema as the fix
Flags the empty catch as swallowing errors
Flags `as Size` on parsed JSON as an unproven cast and recommends validating with the module's schema
Flags the default export in favour of a named export
Every rewrite is TypeScript; no finding cites the Swift, Kotlin or Python references

evals.prompt: The segmentation worker's /segment route in workers/ml/segmentation/src/ai_stylist_segmentation/routes.py is getting long. Refactor it to be cleaner and more idiomatic, and make sure the model inference doesn't block anything.
evals.expected_output: The agent loads only the Python reference, moves logic out of the route into a typed plain function, keeps Pydantic models at the edge, moves blocking inference off the event loop (anyio.to_thread / run_in_threadpool), keeps narrow excepts with `from err`, and validates with `just lint`, `just typecheck` and `just test workers`.
assertions: The agent cites .agents/skills/code-quality/references/python.md and no other language reference
Blocking or CPU-heavy work inside `async def` is moved off the event loop or the route is made sync, with the reason stated
Every new or changed function signature is fully type-annotated using `X | None` and builtin generics
No bare `except:` or `except Exception: pass` is introduced
The report names `just lint`, `just typecheck` and `just test workers` as validation
